Privacy.title: Privacy Policy
Privacy.description: This Privacy Policy explains how Excellence AI accesses, collects, uses, stores, shares, protects, retains, and deletes personal data — including Google user data from Gmail and Google Drive.

Terms.title: Terms of Service
Terms.description: The terms for using Excellence AI. The service is an invitation-only enterprise workspace, not a public consumer chatbot.

Home.badge: Enterprise MCP server · Operated in the EU
Home.heroBody: Excellence AI is an enterprise MCP server: the secure, standard connection between AI tools and company systems. Your team keeps its familiar tools; you control access, approvals, and the audit trail.
Home.featureMcpBody: No new chatbot to roll out. Your team keeps working in the AI tools they know, while Excellence AI connects them securely to company systems.
Home.featureAccessBody: You decide who can access each company system. Sensitive actions only run after a human approves them.
Home.featureAuditBody: Every AI action is logged: who asked for it, which data was accessed, and what happened. Everything can be reviewed later.
Home.featureAdminBody: Company administrators manage AI agents, system connections, roles, and autonomy. Only approved capabilities are available.
Home.featureModelsBody: Claude, Hermes, ChatGPT, Gemini, or Grok — your team uses what works. Company governance always stays in Excellence AI.
Home.howStep1Body: Give them a job description, pick an AI model, and grant access to your company systems.
Home.howStep2Body: Choose which colleagues work with each AI teammate and who counts as their report.
Home.howStep3Title: The team connects its AI tools
Home.howStep3Body: One secure company MCP address. Claude Code, Hermes, ChatGPT, or any MCP-compatible client — the same connection.
Home.howStep4Title: A human decides at the sensitive points
Home.howStep4Body: File writes, folder creation, outbound actions: an approval card, one click.
Home.howStep5Body: See what AI teammates did, when, and which data they touched — costs stay visible too.
Home.howStep6Body: Add knowledge and refine their role so they become more useful to the team.
Home.aboutBody: Excellence AI connects your team's AI tools to company systems. The company manages access, approvals, and audit in one place, while employees keep working in the tools they already know.
Home.aboutCardLead: <brand>Excellence AI</brand> is an enterprise MCP server operated by Excellence Pay Kft. It gives any MCP-compatible AI governed access to company systems — with a full audit trail, privacy safeguards, and human approval.
Home.aboutCardRest: The service is a closed, invitation-only enterprise workspace, not a public chatbot. External account connections are always optional; see the <privacy>Privacy Policy</privacy> and <terms>Terms</terms> for details.
Home.ctaTitle: Every MCP-compatible AI. One control point.
Home.ctaBody: Sign in and connect your team's AI tools to company systems.

account.title: Linked accounts
account.body: Connect your own Gmail and Drive accounts for the AI teammate. You can connect more than one — for example personal and work — and label them so the teammate knows which to use.

operations.title: Waiting on you
operations.body: Two lists: writes a teammate would send in your name, and tasks handed off to you. Both wait for your decision.
operations.approvalsBody: These are writes the teammate would send in your name (for example an API call or a Google Drive file). After approval the system runs the request once; rejection performs no write.
operations.rejected: Rejected. No folder was created on Google Drive.
operations.historyBody: Approved and rejected writes — paginated; loads when you expand.

projects.body: A project holds shared work files (plans, notes, drafts) and the teammates’ approved continuity knowledge: decisions, open tasks, findings. Pick a project and a teammate, then browse or edit memories.

skills.title: Skills
skills.body: A skill is a written workflow: it tells the AI teammate how to do a recurring job. On its own it cannot act — what it can actually do depends on the permissions given to the agent.
skills.hint: Every change starts as a proposal (proposed), and only becomes live (active) after approval — you can always roll back to an earlier version.
skills.migrateHint: If you just pulled new code, run the migration (npx prisma migrate deploy), then restart the dev server.
skills.needOperator: Viewing skills requires at least operator access.

knowledge.title: Knowledge base
knowledge.body: A shared document library: upload once, then attach it on an agent’s page to whoever needs it. Attachment copies the document — later catalog updates do not overwrite the copy on the agent.
knowledge.needOperator: Viewing the knowledge base requires at least operator access.
knowledge.loadFailed: The catalog could not be loaded.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.body: Append-only, hash-chained event log of the organization’s MCP and approval actions. Tokens and secrets are not stored in metadata.

settings.body: This workspace’s own behaviour. The Google OAuth client lives under Platform · Settings; menu visibility is on the Menu access page.

settings.modelsEmpty: No model is allowed yet, so teammates cannot answer. Tick at least one.
settings.modelsCustomBody: If it is missing from the list above, enter the exact model name for that provider (for example anthropic/claude-sonnet-4 on OpenRouter).
settings.modelsNeedAdmin: Admin access is required to change this.
settings.modelsLoadFailed: Could not load the allowed models.
settings.modelsSaveFailed: Could not save the allowed models.
settings.openrouterBody: This key pays for the company’s model usage. Teammates do not need a key on their own computer — calls go through the platform.
settings.openrouterSaved: Key saved. From the next model call, teammates use the company account.
settings.openrouterInvalid: This does not look like an OpenRouter key. It should start with sk-or-.
settings.openrouterLoadFailed: Could not check whether the key is set.
settings.openrouterNeedAdmin: Only an administrator can add this key.
settings.languageBody: Skill descriptions and other human-readable text are written in this language. JSON keys stay in English.

settings.mcpIntroSaved: MCP introduction saved. AI clients will see it on the next connection.

menuAccess.title: Who sees which menu
menuAccess.body: Set which menu items and submenus each role sees in the header. By default everyone sees the full menu for their role — hide items that are not part of that role’s daily work.
menuAccess.help: A checkmark means that role sees the item in the header. Unchecking only removes it from the menu — the page’s access gate stays the same, so this is housekeeping, not an access restriction. If a role cannot reach a page anyway, that cell is not editable.
menuAccess.lockedTitle: This cannot be hidden from administrators — otherwise the menu could not be restored.
menuAccess.noAccessTitle: The {role} role cannot see this page because of its permissions.
menuAccess.savedEmpty: Saved. Every role sees the full menu allowed by its permissions.
menuAccess.saved: Saved. It applies to affected users from the next page load.

platformTenants.title: Workspaces
platformTenants.body: Customer (workspace) registry and lifecycle. Each workspace has its own agents, connectors, playbooks, and audit view — there is no data sharing between workspaces.

platformIam.title: Platform IAM
platformIam.body: Platform-level roles and the audit trail of workspace lifecycle / superadmin assume. A platform role is not a workspace role — a superadmin may enter workspace data only after an explicit, audited assume.

platformSettings.title: Settings
platformSettings.body: Clerk/OAuth, Google Drive, and Google API client settings, the NAV Online Invoice software identity, and the model-session signing key.
platformSettings.fallbackBody: If a provider goes down, the system first tries the teammate’s own backup models, then this shared list — but only models the company has allowed. The switch is written to the log.

platformSettings.fallbackNeedSuperadmin: Superadmin access is required to change this.
platformSettings.fallbackPreviewTitle: What happens if a provider goes down?
platformSettings.fallbackPreviewEmpty: No further shared fallback — if this one fails, only the teammate’s own list remains.
platformSettings.fallbackLoadFailed: Could not load the fallback chain.
platformSettings.fallbackSaveFailed: Could not save the fallback chain.
platformSettings.jwtBody: The platform uses this key to sign model sessions. Every workspace shares it — this is a platform setting, not a company one. It never goes onto teammates’ computers.
platformSettings.jwtReplaceWarn: After a replacement, teammates who are already signed in must sign in again.
platformSettings.jwtSaved: Key saved. It applies from the next sign-in.
platformSettings.jwtInvalid: The key must be at least 32 characters.
platformSettings.jwtLoadFailed: Could not check whether the key is set.

GetStarted.codexBody: Paste the command into the terminal. Browser sign-in opens; use the same account you are using here.
GetStarted.cursorBody: The button opens Cursor and offers to install the server. Then sign in in the browser.
GetStarted.cursorFallback: If the button does not work, you can add the MCP URL above by hand in Cursor settings.
GetStarted.grokBody: Paste the command into the terminal. On first connect, sign in in the browser with your platform account.
GetStarted.grokHint: In Grok you can also open sign-in via /mcps → server → i.
GetStarted.claudeDesc: Add a connector in the app
GetStarted.claudeBody: Open Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector. For the name enter: {name}, for the URL paste:
GetStarted.claudeAfter: Then sign in with the same account you are using here.
GetStarted.claudeCodeBody: Paste the command into the terminal, then complete the sign-in Claude Code offers.
GetStarted.claudeCodeHint: This command is for Claude Code. For Claude Desktop use the guide above.
GetStarted.gooseDesc: Remote MCP extension in the app
GetStarted.gooseStep1: Open the Goose sidebar, then choose Extensions → Add custom extension.
GetStarted.gooseStep2: For type, choose the Streamable HTTP remote extension.
GetStarted.gooseStep3: For the id enter: {name}; for the name: Excellence AI. The server URL is:
GetStarted.gooseAfter: Click Add, then sign in with your platform account in the browser that opens.
GetStarted.step2Body: Open the connected AI tool and ask: “Who am I, and what AI teammates do I have?” If your teammates appear, the connection works.
GetStarted.reopenHint: You can reopen this page from the header at any time.
GetStarted.hermesDesc: With your own model key, for a quick try
GetStarted.hermesIntro: In Hermes Desktop every AI coworker gets its own Bot, with its role and skills. The Bot works through the platform, so you see and approve the work here and no passwords are stored on your machine. No plugin needed: stock Hermes is enough.
GetStarted.hermesStep1Body: Download it from the official site (version 0.21.5 or later) and start it.
GetStarted.hermesStep2Body: On first start Hermes walks you through choosing an AI model and entering its API key. You can change this later in Settings → Model.
GetStarted.hermesStep2Hint: Bots receive only this provider's key. Your other keys stay in the default profile.
GetStarted.hermesStep3Body: Click the button below. Hermes Desktop opens and asks you to confirm the server — check that the name is excellence. Then click Authorize; your browser opens. Sign in with the same account you use here.
GetStarted.hermesStep3Manual: If the button does nothing: Capabilities → MCP → Import, paste your organization MCP URL from above, name the server excellence, choose OAuth, save, then Authorize.
GetStarted.hermesStep3Hint: Keep the server name excellence — Bots reach the platform under this name. In the MCP tab you should see tools listed when the connection works.
GetStarted.hermesAdvancedTerminalBody: If you already use the terminal, you can run this command instead:
GetStarted.hermesStep4Body: In the Hermes chat (default profile), type:
GetStarted.hermesStep4Hint: Hermes creates a Bot for each AI coworker you can access. For each Bot a browser opens once for approval: sign in and accept.
GetStarted.hermesStep5Body: Open Bot Mode. Each coworker shows up as its own Bot, and you can start working in its chat right away.
GetStarted.hermesUpdateBody: If a coworker's role or skills change on the platform, its Bot tells you. Then type the same sentence again in the default profile. Your Bots' chats, avatars and settings are kept.
GetStarted.hermesApprovalHint: Anything a Bot would change (for example sending an email) waits here, on the platform, for your approval.
GetStarted.hermesManagedLimits: In this version, local integration for company sandbox/cloud browser and trusted project roots, website and skill lists need additional implementation; Guard blocks when these are missing. Use company memory tools instead of native local memory. Guard heartbeat checks presence, not hardware attestation. Verify each Hermes version used.
GetStarted.hermesPersonalNote: In this mode you reach the model with your own key, so the company does not see your conversations, only your use of company tools. On a company computer, use Hermes Desktop Enterprise.
GetStarted.hermesEntDesc: Company model key and full company controls
GetStarted.hermesEntIntro: The same Bots, but the platform also provides the model. No model key is stored on your computer, and the company controls and logs AI traffic under its own rules. You do not need to pick a model.
GetStarted.hermesEntAdminTitle: What the admin and IT do
GetStarted.hermesEntAdminNote: Your company admin and IT prepare this: they set the company model key and install the company Hermes settings on your computer. If that has not happened yet, ask them before you start.
GetStarted.hermesEntKeyBody: Bots use the OpenRouter key stored on the platform; no key goes onto employee computers. Add it under Settings → OpenRouter.
GetStarted.hermesEntKeyOk: The company model key is set.
GetStarted.hermesEntKeyMissing: No company model key yet. Until there is one, Bots get no model responses.
GetStarted.hermesEntPolicyBody: Administration → Hermes company controls: select a company default and employee exceptions. Set a ceiling in Tools on the AI coworker page.
GetStarted.hermesEntInstallBody: Pick whose computer gets the company settings. Download the installer, copy it to that computer, and run the command. First grant access to at least one active AI coworker — otherwise the computer blocks all local operations.
GetStarted.hermesEntDownloadFailed: Could not download the installer. Try again.
GetStarted.hermesEntNoMembers: There is no active employee to issue an installer for.
GetStarted.hermesEntInstallRun: Copy the downloaded file to the employee computer, open Terminal in that folder, and run:
GetStarted.hermesEntInstallHint: The installer applies the company settings. Then restart Hermes. The file is small; it is not the Hermes app.
GetStarted.hermesEntSecurityBody: IT should revoke model keys previously stored on the laptop. Company keys stay on the server. Use managed computers without employee admin rights, central deployment and outbound network rules; machine administrators can bypass local controls. Reinstall after new Bot profiles or permission expansion.
GetStarted.hermesEntVerifyBody: After the employee has connected the platform and created the Bots: hermes config must show the managed settings and the excellence provider. Send a test message, check model and tool audit, and test a blocked operation and access revocation. Clients without Guard do not receive company model responses.
GetStarted.hermesEntStep1Body: If IT has not installed it yet, download it from the official site (version 0.21.5 or later). Restart it after the company settings are installed.
GetStarted.hermesEntNoModel: You do not need to enter a model or API key. If Hermes still asks for a key, the company settings are not on your computer yet: ask IT.

AgentLocalRoots.help: Several machines, several paths: one hint per line, for example ~/Projects/platform on a laptop and /home/gery/src/platform on an office box. Not a permission and not ranked — on this host the client opens the folder that exists. In Codex, Claude, and Goose the user opens it. In Hermes, Guard may allowlist the union. Company memory stays on MCP. It takes effect at the next publish.

AgentModelConfig.title: Reasoning engine
AgentModelConfig.help: Choose which AI model powers this teammate. The list is the company’s allowed models. If you leave it unset, the first allowed model runs.
AgentModelConfig.emptyPolicy: No model is allowed yet, so teammates cannot answer. An admin can allow some under Settings → Allowed models.
AgentModelConfig.primaryDisabled: This model is no longer allowed — pick another, or a backup will be used.
AgentModelConfig.fallbacksHelp: If the primary model’s provider is down or overloaded, we try these in order. The switch is written to the log. Mid-conversation, after the first word, we do not switch.
AgentModelConfig.noOwnFallback: No own backup — only the shared chain helps if a provider fails.
AgentModelConfig.previewTitle: What happens if a provider goes down?
AgentModelConfig.previewEmpty: No allowed backup is available — the user will see an error if this one fails.
AgentModelConfig.thinkingLuna: Fast, light thinking — for routine work.
AgentModelConfig.thinkingSol: Deep thinking — for complex, multi-step work.
AgentModelConfig.maxTokensHelp: How long a reply we allow in one turn. The model counts in “tokens” — roughly a short word, or part of a longer word.
AgentModelConfig.needAdmin: Admin access is required to change this.

tenant.label: Tenant
tenant.explanation: Exists only in this workspace. The tenant admin can assign it to their own (non-system) agents. It appears in slash commands on agents it is assigned to.

published.label: Published
published.explanation: A package issued by a platform admin: every workspace can read it, but cannot edit it. The tenant admin can assign it to their own (non-system) agents.

system.label: System
system.explanation: Internal platform skill. It appears only on the selected system agent, and can only be assigned there. A tenant admin cannot put it on another agent.

Provisioning.title: Connectors
Provisioning.tabConnectorsDesc: Active connectors and drafts that are not activated yet.
Provisioning.tabTemplatesSuper: Platform and workspace catalog. A superadmin can add a template to the platform or any workspace; a tenant admin only to their own.
Provisioning.tabTemplatesAdmin: Template catalog. A tenant admin can add a new template to their own workspace.
Provisioning.tabTemplatesView: Template catalog. Create a new connector from these templates.
Provisioning.name: Name
Provisioning.generalHint: From the template catalog or as a custom connection, with the usual onboarding.
Provisioning.openapiKindHint: You need the partner API description link; a key only if the API asks for one. Later changes can be taken over with a button after review.
Provisioning.fromTemplateHint: Pick from the template catalog — the connector takes the template name.
Provisioning.customConnectionHint: No template — custom onboarding from discovery or a document.
Provisioning.usesTemplateName: Name: {name} — we use the template name, you do not need a separate one.
Provisioning.step1Body: Pick the type first. From a template the connector takes the template name; you only name a custom connection.
Provisioning.step2ApiBody: The public API description link is required; a key only if the partner API asks for one. After create, the wizard walks you through link approval, partner trust, looking for updates, and taking the first version.
Provisioning.accessKeyHint: Only needed if the partner API asks for a key. It stays in a secure secret store; it never goes into the database. Leave empty for a public, keyless API.
Provisioning.capabilityOnSync: We download the capability list on the wizard’s “Look for updates” step.
Provisioning.catalogHelp: If the link is a catalog (several API descriptions), you can pick which ones become connections.
Provisioning.singleApi: This is a single API description — create it with the “Create connector” button below.
Provisioning.catalogLeaves: Catalog index ({count} API descriptions) — pick which ones become connections:
Provisioning.sharedKeyHint: One key (e.g. a POSnavigator pn_ key) for every selected API. Each connection gets it in its own secret slot — you can replace them one by one later.
Provisioning.perLeafKeyHint: A separate key can be entered under each selected row.
Provisioning.noKeyHint: For public APIs that do not ask for a key.
Provisioning.itemCreated: {name} created — link approval and trust are still pending.
Provisioning.dualControlHint: The link usually needs another colleague’s approval before we go live — so we do not read from a mistyped or fake address. A platform superadmin can approve and activate alone. The wizard steps are the same as under Details on the card.
Provisioning.step3LinkBody: Check that the partner API description address is correct and from a trusted source.
Provisioning.step4TrustBody: We only download and activate API changes for a partner marked as trusted.
Provisioning.trustAlready: ✓ The partner is already marked as trusted.
Provisioning.step5SyncBody: We download the partner OpenAPI description and build a proposed capability list for the first live version.
Provisioning.versionAlready: ✓ A taken-over version already exists — the connection can be used.
Provisioning.step6ApplyBody: Review the first capability list. Until you approve it, the connection cannot be assigned to an agent.
Provisioning.step2TemplateBody: {name} — set the auth mode and required fields. The connector takes the template name.
Provisioning.templateSelfContained: The template builds a self-contained draft config from provider metadata and instance fields.
Provisioning.driveOauthNeeded: The Google Drive template needs the platform Drive OAuth setup (Platform · Settings → Google Drive OAuth).
Provisioning.googleApiOauthNeeded: The Google API templates (Analytics / Search Console / Ads / Calendar / Sheets) need the platform Google API OAuth setup (Platform · Settings → Google API).
Provisioning.step2CustomBody: The flow takes you to a config candidate. You only create the draft in the next step.
Provisioning.openapiHint: Upload a spec or paste a URL
Provisioning.fromDoc: Generate from an API document (provisioning assistant)
Provisioning.fetchStepBody: Enter the public OpenAPI or API-doc URL. The platform downloads it, you review the content, then the provisioning assistant generates a config candidate.
Provisioning.reviewOrUpload: Step 2 — review or upload a file
Provisioning.onlyOpenApi: OpenAPI JSON/YAML only. We do not extract config from free-text docs right now.
Provisioning.truncated: (truncated — the full spec was too large)
Provisioning.manualDescriptorHint: Paste the JSON, or load the example, then continue to review.
Provisioning.secretNeverHere: The secret NEVER goes here, only the alias name intended for Secret Manager.
Provisioning.secretOnActivate: The credential secret is entered at activation (managed secret store).
Provisioning.materializerHint: The materializer validates fields on the server, then calls the same draft gate.
Provisioning.templateScopeSuper: Choose platform- or workspace-level. Saving creates a new version and runs the materializer self-check.
Provisioning.templateScopeTenant: The template goes into your workspace catalog. Saving creates a new version and runs the materializer self-check.
Provisioning.templateIconHint: The service logo at the front of template and connector cards. Without an image a generic connector icon is shown.
Provisioning.templateIconTooBig: The image must be at most 150 KB.
Provisioning.templateIconInvalid: Only image files can be uploaded.
Provisioning.templatesFromThese: You can create a connector from these templates.
Provisioning.pendingHintMixed: For OpenAPI connections, link approval, partner trust, or taking the first version is still pending. Open the card for the steps.
Provisioning.pendingHint: Link approval, partner trust, or taking the first version is still pending. Open the card for the steps.
Provisioning.gapsHint: These connections are active in the database, but have no provisioning draft or self-updating card (often a migration or old seed leftover). They may still be assignable to an agent; if they are unused, decommission them — audited archive, not a hard delete.
Provisioning.unmanagedHint: There is no management UI for this row on this page — only decommission or platform support (if it needs to go back to a draft/OpenAPI path).
Provisioning.decommissionGapBody: Not a hard delete: after removing agent assignments and the managed secret-ref, the connection becomes archived. Bank-preset / L2–L3 needs a second approver.
Provisioning.reasonGapPlaceholder: E.g. migration leftover, unused http_api connection
Provisioning.confirmDecommNamed: Sure? “{name}” will be torn down and archived.
Provisioning.confirmDecomm: Sure? The connector will be torn down and archived.
Provisioning.sensitivityTitle: We found a sensitive pattern in the content (e.g. email, national ID, tax number).
Provisioning.sensitivityBody: By default only a local model could process it — but API docs often contain dummy/example data. If you are sure it is not real sensitive data, you can continue with an external model.
Provisioning.pendingOp: Waiting because an operation is in progress.
Provisioning.catalogNoSolo: This is a catalog index — create the connections with the leaf picker above; a standalone “Create connector” cannot run here.
Provisioning.fillRequired: Fill in the template’s required fields.
Provisioning.needConfig: Generate or provide a config descriptor first.
Provisioning.needDocUrl: Enter the API-doc or OpenAPI URL.
Provisioning.fileTooBig: The file is larger than 2 MiB.
Provisioning.onlyOpenApiFile: Only an OpenAPI JSON/YAML file can be uploaded.
Provisioning.invalidJson: The config is not valid JSON.
Provisioning.invalidTemplateJson: The template descriptor is not valid JSON.
Provisioning.pickTenantForTemplate: Choose a workspace for a workspace-level template.
Provisioning.needAtLeastOne: Pick at least one API description from the list.
Provisioning.needLeafNames: Give every selected row a name.
Provisioning.catalogNotSoloCreate: This is a catalog index — a standalone connection cannot be created from it. Use the “Create selected connections” button above.
Provisioning.sensitiveFound: We found a sensitive pattern in the document. If it is dummy/example data, you can continue with the button.
Provisioning.openapiExtracted: OpenAPI spec detected — config candidate extracted deterministically. Review it, then create the draft.
Provisioning.docFetchedTrunc: Document downloaded (truncated because of the size limit). Check the content, then generate a config candidate.
Provisioning.docFetched: Document downloaded. Check the content below, then click Generate config candidate.
Provisioning.fileLoaded: File loaded. Check the content, then generate a config candidate.
Provisioning.singleNotCatalog: This is a single API description, not a catalog index — you can use the plain “Create connector”.
Provisioning.catalogFound: Catalog index: {count} API descriptions in it. Pick which ones become connections.
Provisioning.batchAllOk: {count} connections created. You still need to approve the links and partner trust on the panel before you can look for updates.
Provisioning.batchPartial: {ok}/{total} connections created — see the failed rows below.
Provisioning.createdNeedLink: Connection created — the link still needs approval.
Provisioning.draftFromTemplate: Draft connector created from the template.
Provisioning.trustFailed: Marking the partner as trusted failed.
Provisioning.trusted: The partner is marked as trusted.
Provisioning.openapiLive: The OpenAPI connection is active and usable.
Provisioning.templateSaved: Connector template saved as a new version.
Provisioning.autoApproveOn: The workspace allowed limited automatic take-over.
Provisioning.autoApproveOff: Automatic take-over is off for the workspace.
Provisioning.activateKeylessBody: You did not enter an API key or a valid secret reference. Activate without a key anyway? Agent calls will fail auth until then.
Provisioning.activateKeylessShort: You did not enter an API key or a valid secret reference. Activate without a key anyway?
Provisioning.configUpdated: Config updated — validation/review/sandbox reset, run the gate again.
Provisioning.deleteNeverActivated: Permanent delete — only for a connector that was never activated. The broken connector and draft row are deleted; this cannot be undone.
Provisioning.reopened: Connector reopened as a draft — edit it, then activate again.
Provisioning.egressAdded: Egress host added to the allowlist: {host} — revalidated.
Provisioning.oauthSecretPlaceholder: Client secret of the OAuth app registered with the provider
Provisioning.rawKeyPlaceholder: Raw key generated in the external system
Provisioning.oauthSecretHint: The client secret goes into the managed secret store (secret-ref). The key is stored encrypted and never lands in the database.
Provisioning.rawKeyHint: Enter only the raw key — the system adds the “Bearer " prefix (for the bearer scheme). The key is stored encrypted and never lands in the database.
Provisioning.clientIdPlaceholder: client_id of the OAuth app registered with the provider
Provisioning.agentOwnedKey: Enter a key → this agent gets its own key
Provisioning.reasonActivePlaceholder: E.g. misconfigured egress host, replaced provider
Provisioning.editResetsGates: Saving resets the gate: validation, review, and the sandbox test will all run again before the connector can be activated.
Provisioning.unreadableConfig: The stored config cannot be parsed.
Provisioning.cannotEditLive: An active connector’s config cannot be rewritten live. To fix it, reopen as a draft: the connector goes offline (the Tool Broker will not resolve it), then you must walk validation→review→sandbox→activation again. Agent assignments stay, and return on reactivation.
Provisioning.deleteDraftBody: Permanent hard-delete — only for a never-activated draft. The broken draft connector and draft row are deleted for good (the delete is audited).
Provisioning.warningsFixable: Some of the warnings can be fixed in the draft config. After the change the gates restart, so the new config must be validated again.
Provisioning.newEgressHosts: New egress host(s) — add them to the allowlist before activation (§9, audited admin act):
Provisioning.notValidatedYet: The draft is not validated yet. Run the validator before sandbox test, review, or activation.
Provisioning.reviewBody: Final human approval that also considers the sandbox test. This gate only makes sense in draft. On an active connector you need revoke or a new version, not a later review rewrite.
Provisioning.sandboxBody: A narrow, non-live probe call. Activation stays blocked without a successful test.
Provisioning.activatePrereqs: Activation requires: non-failed validation, a successful sandbox test, and an approved review.
Provisioning.gmailOauthOk: The platform Google OAuth app is configured — Client ID and Secret are not needed at workspace level.
Provisioning.gmailOauthNeed: The Gmail connector uses the platform Google OAuth app. Before activation a platform admin must set it on Platform · Settings → Google OAuth.
Provisioning.driveOauthOk: The platform Google Drive OAuth app is configured — Client ID and Secret are not needed at workspace level.
Provisioning.driveOauthNeed: The Google Drive connector uses the platform Drive OAuth app. Before activation a platform admin must set it on Platform · Settings → Google Drive OAuth.
Provisioning.googleApiOauthOk: The platform Google API OAuth app is configured (Analytics / Search Console / Ads / Calendar / Sheets) — Client ID and Secret are not needed at workspace level.
Provisioning.googleApiOauthNeed: The Google API connector uses the platform Google API OAuth app. Before activation set it on Platform · Settings → Google API.
Provisioning.existingSecretHint: If you already store the secret elsewhere, reference it here instead of typing a key. Accepted forms: env:NAME, secret-manager:projects/…/secrets/<id>, secret-ref:<id>. Otherwise leave empty and type the key above.
Provisioning.badAlias: Alias form not accepted. Use an env:, secret-manager:, or secret-ref: prefix — or leave empty and type the key above.
Provisioning.actingUser: Acting user email (registered in the CRM — X-Acting-User header)
Provisioning.actingUserNeeded: A CRM-registered acting user email is required for the keyed test.
Provisioning.addToOauthApp: (add it to the OAuth app settings)
Provisioning.keylessWarn: You can activate without a key, but we ask for confirmation — the agent will not call successfully until then.
Provisioning.assignToAgent: Assign to an agent (human admin act)
Provisioning.perAgentKeyHint: (agent_owned — optional if you use the connector’s shared key)
Provisioning.decommissionActiveBody: Not a hard delete: after removing agent assignments, recomputing those agents’ http_api capabilities, revoking active user grants, and deleting the managed secret-ref, the connector becomes archived — the connector row and audit history stay. The act cannot be undone (you would have to activate again). Bank-preset / L2–L3 needs a second approver.
Provisioning.httpApiViaEditor: This connector was set up through the “API connector” editor (http_api runtime config).
Provisioning.oauthClientId: OAuth client ID (not a secret → config)
Provisioning.fromTemplateShortHint: Pick from the template catalog — the connector takes the template name.
Provisioning.customShortHint: No template — custom onboarding from discovery or a document.

ClientPolicy.title: Hermes company controls
ClientPolicy.body: Set what employees can do with AI. Customize the company default per employee; the AI coworker ceiling always applies.
ClientPolicy.empty: No employee has custom settings yet; everyone inherits the company default: {preset}.
ClientPolicy.presetHelp: Bound: sensitive data; Standard: office work; Free: development. Individual overrides remain when you change the preset.
ClientPolicy.agentHelp: This is a ceiling: stricter employee settings still apply. It takes effect without republishing the AI coworker.
ClientPolicy.saveFailed: Saving failed. Do not treat these settings as saved; try again.
ClientPolicy.conflict: Someone changed these settings. Reload the page and review the latest values.
ClientPolicy.widenWarning: This employee would receive more freedom than the company default in the areas below. The exception is audited separately.
ClientPolicy.confirmWidening: I approve this employee exception to the company default.
ClientPolicy.effectiveNotice: Changes apply in the next Hermes session; revocations apply on the next request. If the installed machine settings blocked a newly allowed feature, download and reinstall the machine package.
ClientPolicy.downloadFailed: Could not download the installer. Check access and try again.
ClientPolicy.floorHelp: On the employee computer run: sudo bash excellence-telepito.sh. First steps has the same installer. Issuing a changed package disables company model access for the old machine settings until installation.

help.sandbox_only: Local execution is blocked; use the company sandbox tool.
help.local_with_approval: Runs on the employee computer after approval for each command.
help.local_free: Local execution is allowed; the general approval rule still applies.
help.none: This setting grants no access or requires no additional approval.
help.read_only: Local files may be read, but cannot be changed.
help.project_write: Trusted project root checks are not connected yet; this version blocks local writes at this level.
help.free: No additional limit for this capability; other company rules still apply.
help.company_cloud: The local browser is blocked; connecting the cloud browser is a separate implementation step.
help.domain_allowlist: The local browser is blocked until a trusted website list is connected.
help.company_egress: Search through the company connection instead of the built-in local search.
help.builtin: The built-in Hermes web search can be used.
help.company_only: Tools may only be called through the company Excellence system.
help.plus_approved: External connections require a separately approved tool rule.
help.approved_only: Local skill loading is blocked until a trusted skill list is connected; company tools remain available.
help.plus_own_audited: Own skills may be used; operations are audited.
help.excellence: Use Excellence tools for company memory; native local memory is blocked.
help.local: Hermes memory stored on the employee computer may be used.
help.audited: Autonomous or scheduled tasks may run with audit logging.
help.always: Every permitted operation requires human approval.
help.risky: Changing or risky operations require human approval.
help.plus_tool_results: Conversation content and tool results are recorded.
help.prompt_and_response: Model request and response content are recorded.
help.metadata: Records who used which model or tool and when, without content.
help.block: A detected value prevents the request from reaching the model.
help.tokenize: The model sees a surrogate; supported values are restored in the response.
help.warn: The request may proceed; detection is audited.
help.off: This category filter does not restrict outgoing content.

ClientPolicy.filterLimits: Data protection: this version detects known patterns and restores email and person names learned from email headers. Other detected types are blocked instead of tokenized. Automatic company-name and arbitrary person-name detection is not connected yet.
ClientPolicy.noFileHelp: Local files cannot be read or written.
ClientPolicy.noApprovalHelp: This setting requires no additional approval; other operation limits apply.

Onboarding.companyBody: A few details and your own workspace is ready. You will be the company’s first administrator.
Onboarding.displayNameHint: This is how it appears in the app and in invitations.
Onboarding.taxIdHelp: Needed for invoicing later. Not required now — you can add it any time.
Onboarding.terms: I accept the <gtc>Terms and Conditions</gtc> and the <privacy>Privacy Notice</privacy>.
Onboarding.capReachedTitle: You have reached the company limit
Onboarding.capReachedBody: One account can start at most {cap} companies of its own. To start a new one, an earlier one has to be closed — we are happy to help.
Onboarding.assumedTitle: You are acting inside another company
Onboarding.assumedBody: You can’t start your own company in platform supervision mode. Exit to platform mode and start it from there.
Onboarding.inviteChoiceBody: An invitation was sent to {email}. If you belong there, join — you’ll work in the same space as your colleagues.
Onboarding.teamBody: {company} is ready. Send invitations to your colleagues — they get a sign-in link by email. You can also do this later.
Onboarding.inviteRoleHelp: Operator: works with AI colleagues. Approver: also approves sensitive actions. Viewer: read-only. Administrator: can configure everything.

errors.terms_required: Please accept the Terms and the Privacy Notice to continue.
errors.name_too_long: The company name is too long.
errors.tax_id_too_long: The tax number can be at most 32 characters.
errors.user_not_found: We can’t find your account. Please sign in again.
errors.user_suspended: A suspended account can’t start a company.
errors.assumed_context: You can’t start your own company in platform supervision mode.
errors.cap_reached: You have reached the company limit (at most {cap}).
errors.slug_exhausted: We couldn’t create the company with this name right now. Try a slightly different name.
errors.unavailable: Starting a company is not available right now. Please try again later.
errors.invitation: This invitation is no longer valid (expired, revoked or already used).
errors.invalid_email: Please enter a valid email address.
errors.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.
